xdrivers.method: X search (relevancy, last ~5 days) + X news; explanations are inferred, not confirmed

MU.explanation: Likely: MU's last session was Fri Oct 16, down about 5.6% near $879 and about 14.6% lower over 5 days, as a broad AI and chip selloff hit a memory group already rattled by China CXMT's DRAM progress. Over the weekend X buzzed about a 'Black Monday' as thin weekend trading in tokenized and perpetual versions knocked memory names lower again, while bulls pointed to JPMorgan calling for a memory re-rating and KeyBanc expecting DRAM prices to rise 15–20% in Q4.

sources.gist: JPMorgan calls for a re-rating of memory stocks: a deepening supply-demand gap, rising AI capex, more HBM per accelerator, and HBM4E using about 4x the wafers per bit
KeyBanc's John Vinh, after Asia supply-chain checks, expects Micron DRAM prices up 15–20% in Q4, NAND up 20%, and HBM up 80–100% in Q1 2027
Weekend trading showed memory names lower before Monday's open (WDC −5.7%, STX −4.5%, SNDK −3.4%, MU −3.2%) amid widespread Black Monday calls
A sudden weekend crash in Binance's TradFi perpetuals hit BTC and ETH, and AI-related stock perps dropped about 5% within seconds

SPCX.explanation: Likely: SPCX's last session was Fri Oct 16, down about 1.7% near $146 and about 10% lower over 5 days, as Tesla–SpaceX merger buzz failed to lift it in a risk-off tech tape. Weekend X chatter shifted to Tuesday's Oct 20 earnings, the day before Tesla's, and to exchange-ratio math, with a widely viewed post arguing a $420 Tesla valuation would be about an 18% premium to Friday's ratio.

sources.gist: Merger math: at $420 per Tesla, each Tesla would convert to 2.88 SpaceX vs 2.43 at Friday's close, about an 18% premium
Thread arguing a SpaceX–Tesla combination could hand Musk majority control of Tesla through the way SpaceX stock is structured
Notes SpaceX's COO started following Tesla and hopes for a merger announcement around back-to-back earnings (SpaceX Tue, Tesla Wed)
Earnings preview: SpaceX reports Tue Oct 20 with consensus EPS about $0.14 on revenue about $12.9B (FactSet), up from $7.81B in Q2

TSLA.explanation: Likely: TSLA's last session was Fri Oct 16, down about 2.1% near $355 and about 7.3% lower over 5 days, as the Roadster-reveal pop reversed in the tech selloff. Weekend X focus moved to Oct 21 Q3 earnings, with tastylive calling it the Mag 7's worst performer and noting earnings are expected to fall about 10% despite the deliveries beat, while others flagged robotaxi miles and FSD subscriptions as the numbers to watch.

sources.gist: The Roadster got airborne but TSLA still closed lower; the Mag 7's worst performer faces earnings expected to fall 10% even after a deliveries beat
Q3 earnings Oct 21: watching unsupervised robotaxi miles (about 380K last quarter) and active FSD subscriptions (1.48M) over deliveries
Flying-Roadster hype into earnings sets up volatility, but a halo product isn't a re-rating; deliveries and margins still matter
Kalshi odds of a Tesla–SpaceX merger before March jumped to 56% from 29% on Oct 16, yet neither stock rallied

LMND.explanation: No clear X driver for the session. LMND fell about 3.6% on Fri Oct 16 (about 4.9% lower over 5 days), giving back most of the pop around the Lemonade Agentic launch; weekend X was quiet apart from a chart account calling a breakdown, so the dip likely tracked the broad growth and tech selloff.

sources.gist: Lemonade announced Lemonade Agentic, opening Lemonade OS so customers' AI agents can manage their coverage
Lemonade Agentic lets a personal AI agent buy, manage, renew and file claims with no forms or calls
Chart view: LMND breaking lower near $44.20 on low volume and not yet oversold; sees further downside toward $39

UPST.explanation: No clear X driver. UPST fell about 4.8% on Fri Oct 16, giving back about half of Oct 15's jump and leaving it about 2.2% lower over 5 days; X chatter centered on macro, with the 10-year yield peaking near 4.92% on Oct 16 and fintech lagging badly over the past year.

sources.gist: Draws parallels to past tops: the 10-year yield climbed from 3.5% in March to a 4.92% peak on Oct 16 as AI profitability questions grew
Fintech has been brutal: iShares Fintech Active ETF is down 22% over 12 months while the Nasdaq 100 is up 21%
Argues bearish traders are crowded as liquidity rotates from AI into fintech, and Upstart can come out stronger

UMAC.explanation: No clear X driver. UMAC dropped about 8.5% on Fri Oct 16 and is down roughly 22% over 5 days, with no negative company news visible on X; holders described a punishing tape for growth and defense names and were waiting on news, and the main company item remained CEO Allan Evans being named chairman of XTI Aerospace.

sources.gist: Describes 'growth and defense stock hell' with endless red days while the stock trades at a big discount
Says the company needs to release news to turn the stock around
CEO Allan Evans named chairman of XTI Aerospace, in which Unusual Machines holds roughly a 34% stake

BLZE.explanation: No clear X driver for the session. BLZE fell about 13% on Fri Oct 16 and is down roughly 32% over 5 days; X tied the Oct 14 plunge of about 22% to its CoreWeave exposure (CoreWeave is described as a major customer), and Friday's drop showed up mainly on top-decliner lists without fresh company news.

sources.gist: BLZE got caught in the CoreWeave crossfire since CoreWeave is a major customer; bull case is Backblaze becoming a meaningful AI-storage platform at about a $600M market cap
Calls Backblaze a storage version of a neocloud, dragged down with its CoreWeave relationship while undercutting giants on price
Lists BLZE among the Oct 16 session's biggest decliners at about −14%

OSCR.explanation: No clear X driver for the session. OSCR fell about 4.7% on Fri Oct 16 (about 4.4% lower over 5 days) with no fresh negative headline on X; weekend chatter stayed bullish, citing a 2027 entry into South Carolina's ACA marketplace and a post claiming 2026 operating-earnings guidance is now $600–800M, up from $250–450M, ahead of Nov 5 Q3 results.

sources.gist: Says 2026 earnings-from-operations guidance was raised to $600–800M from an original $250–450M and expects a big beat
Oscar is entering South Carolina's ACA marketplace in 2027 in six counties, targeting 400–600 more counties by 2029
Chart view: expects OSCR to run if it breaks above its $37 IPO-era highs

BTC-USD.explanation: Likely: Bitcoin rose about 1% on the Oct 18 UTC day to about $82.2K (about −1% over 5 days), recovering from a weekend flash crash that started in Binance's TradFi perpetuals. X framed the move as stabilization rather than risk-on, with spot BTC ETFs seeing about −$228M net outflows for Oct 12–16 and Sunday-night US futures opening green.

sources.gist: BTC back above $82K, up about 0.9% on the day, but it looks more like stabilization than a real risk-on move
Spot BTC ETFs had about −$228M net flows for Oct 12–16 with 3 red days of 5; Friday alone −$82.4M led by IBIT
A sudden weekend crash in Binance's TradFi perpetuals hit BTC, ETH and AI-stock perps within seconds
Sunday-night US futures opened green and the VIX cooled, deflating the Black Monday hype

rebellionaire.overview: Rebellionaire (rebellionaire.com) is a Tesla-focused advisory firm led by Bradford Ferguson. It writes for concentrated investors and promotes covered calls and a trim-and-add discipline. Broad views: strongly bullish on Tesla (Robotaxi, Optimus, energy). It favors a Tesla-SpaceX combination only at a fair exchange ratio, ideally after Tesla's autonomy value is priced in. It runs a SpaceX hub covering the June 12 IPO and is bullish on Micron's AI-memory profits. It is a long-time Lemonade bull, covers Upstart every quarter, and has little crypto coverage.

MU.title: What Terafab Means for Micron and the Memory Tradeade and Micron Holders
MU.author: Rebellionaire Staff
MU.summary: Terafab (Tesla/SpaceX/xAI fab; Intel joined Apr 7) plans memory as well as logic. They see no near-term hit to Micron since volume is 2027+ and HBM later. Bull case: Micron becomes the US HBM partner. Bear case: Terafab builds its own DRAM over a decade.

MU.title: Intel Joins Terafab: What It Means for Tesla Investors
MU.author: Rebellionaire Staff
MU.summary: Intel joins Terafab for design, fab and packaging. Plan: 100K wafer starts/month at pilot scaling to 1M, and 100-200B AI and memory chips a year. The $20-25B cost is not yet in Tesla's 2026 capex.

MU.title: Micron vs Tesla: The Profit Shock Nobody Sees
MU.author: Rebellionaire Staff
MU.summary: Argues Micron's next-quarter net income will top any Tesla quarter through 2030. Cites ~$24B revenue, 74.4% gross margin and $12 EPS, plus guidance of $33.5B, 81% GM and ~$19 EPS, with the stock near 4x forward P/E. Says the shortage makes memory no longer a commodity.

SPCX.title: Terafab & Orbital AI Compute: The Real Risks
SPCX.author: Rebellionaire Staff
SPCX.summary: Risk-focused piece separating two bets: Terafab (vertical integration into chipmaking) and orbital AI compute (moving workloads to space). Launch and reuse are proven; chipmaking at scale is unproven and capital-heavy.

SPCX.title: SPCX Position Sizing: A Framework for Concentrated SpaceX Holders
SPCX.author: Rebellionaire Staff
SPCX.summary: Framework for concentrated SPCX investors after the IPO: split risk into company, liquidity and behavioral, and set trim and add bands in advance rather than defaulting to diversification.

SPCX.title: SpaceX IPO S-1: What Tesla Investors Need to Know
SPCX.author: Rebellionaire Staff
SPCX.summary: S-1 readout: 2025 revenue ~$18.7B, Q1 2026 net loss ~$4.9B, Starlink ~10.3M subscribers and ~$7.2B 2025 segment EBITDA, AI segment ~$6.4B operating loss. Calls the viral claim that Tesla investors would 'only get 30%' in a combination wrong.

SPCX.title: SpaceX xAI Merger: Why Wall Street Is Paying Attention
SPCX.author: Rebellionaire Staff
SPCX.summary: SpaceX acquired xAI at ~$1T / ~$250B (~$1.25T combined), with xAI reportedly burning ~$1B a month. Bull case: internal funding. Bear case: two capital-hungry businesses stacked together.

TSLA.title: Tesla SpaceX Merger: Why Timing Matters for Tesla Shareholders
TSLA.author: Rebellionaire Staff
TSLA.summary: Backs a Tesla-SpaceX combination strategically but says the exchange ratio is everything. Tesla investors should want Robotaxi and Optimus valued before a deal, and they think the market gives Optimus near-zero credit.

TSLA.title: What If Tesla Flips the SpaceX Deal?
TSLA.author: Rebellionaire Staff
TSLA.summary: If Tesla proves Robotaxi, Optimus and AI profits first, it could enter a SpaceX deal as the stronger half. Calls Robotaxi the cleanest catalyst because it turns autonomy into revenue.

TSLA.title: Tesla’s SpaceX Problem: The Ratio Matters
TSLA.author: Rebellionaire Staff
TSLA.summary: With Tesla at ~$1.4-1.7T and SpaceX at ~$1.75T, the gap between 51% and 40% ownership matters. Musk's >50% SpaceX voting control makes the ratio the key fairness test.

TSLA.title: Tesla's Biggest Fixable Weakness Isn't the Car
TSLA.author: Rebellionaire Staff
TSLA.summary: Optimus production at Fremont late Jul/Aug 2026, with Giga Texas volume ~summer 2027. 2025 energy revenue $12.8B (+27%), 46.7 GWh deployed. Argues vague timelines are a fixable drag on valuation.

TSLA.title: How Tesla Plans to Mass-Produce the Cybercab Without the 2,500-Unit Cap
TSLA.author: Rebellionaire Staff
TSLA.summary: Explains how a 2022 NHTSA rule could let the wheel-less Cybercab scale past the 2,500-unit exemption cap. Production was targeted for Q2 2026. Relevant to the current NHTSA certification probe.

LMND.title: Berkshire’s AI Blind Spot in Insurance
LMND.author: Rebellionaire Staff
LMND.summary: Uses Ajit Jain's AI comments to argue legacy insurers trail AI-first Lemonade, since small-premium policies can't absorb human claim handling.

LMND.title: Lemonade Offering Tesla Autonomous Insurance
LMND.author: Rebellionaire Staff
LMND.summary: Lemonade launched autonomous car insurance starting with Tesla FSD, with per-mile rates ~50% lower for FSD-engaged miles, priced from vehicle data.

LMND.title: Everyone’s Looking for the Next Tesla—Here’s What They Miss
LMND.author: Rebellionaire Staff
LMND.summary: After Lemonade's $20-to-$60 run, argues the next leg comes from improving loss ratios, newer lines and operating leverage.

LMND.title: Inside Lemonade’s AI Automation Shift in Tel Aviv
LMND.author: Rebellionaire Staff
LMND.summary: Community notes from a Tel Aviv event: >60% of support tickets and ~57% of claims handled end-to-end by AI (event notes, not company filings).

UPST.title: Upstart Q1 2026: Strong Quarter, Messy Message
UPST.author: Henry Dierkes
UPST.summary: Q1 2026: revenue $308M (+44%), originations $3.4B (+61%), GAAP loss of $0.07 per share, adj. EBITDA $40.5M, contribution margin down from 55% to 50%. Full-year guidance reaffirmed.

UPST.title: Upstart Q1 2026 Results: Strong, Messy, Misread
UPST.author: Henry Dierkes
UPST.summary: Says Q1 was stronger than the market reaction implied; reaffirmed guidance was the biggest positive. Debate centers on EPS, balance-sheet loans and communication.

UPST.title: Upstart Q1 2026 Preview: All Systems Gu?
UPST.author: Henry Dierkes
UPST.summary: Q4 2025 recap: revenue $296M (+35%), GAAP net income $18.6M, balance-sheet loans cut $245M, 70% of auto and HELOC funding from partners.

UPST.title: It's Gu Time: A Conversation With Upstart's Incoming CEO
UPST.author: Henry Dierkes
UPST.summary: Interview with incoming CEO Paul Gu covering Model 25, the Upstart Macro Index (est. to have avoided ~80% of 2022 disruption), his ~$4M open-market stock purchase and ~35% annual compounding guidance.

BTC-USD.title: Trump's U.S. Crypto Reserve: Strategic Genius or Just More Chaos?
